title: Dalihan Na Tolu
description: The fundamental kinship and social philosophy that governs all interpersonal relationships and ceremonies within the Batak society.
detailedContent:
Dalihan Na Tolu translates literally to "The Three-Legged Hearth," referring to the three stones supporting a traditional cooking pot. If one leg is broken or uneven, the pot will tip over. Similarly, Batak society relies on three distinct social relationships:

1. **Somba Marhula-hula** (Honor the Wife-Givers): The Hula-hula are the clan from whom a family received their wives. They are viewed as the source of blessing, vitality, and custom power, and must be treated with supreme respect.
2. **Elek Marboru** (Be Kind and Gentle to the Wife-Takers): The Boru are the family members who married daughters of the clan. They act as the loyal hands, organizers, and executors of all family events, and must be treated with gentle kindness and appreciation.
3. **Manat Mardongan Tubu** (Be Prudent with Male Siblings/Agmates): Dongan Tubu are paternal brothers and brothers-in-clan. Because of equal inheritance and standing, relationships can easily spark friction, demanding constant prudence, polite speech, and cooperation.

This philosophy establishes an elegant, self-regulating social matrix where no person is permanently superior or inferior; in one ceremony a man is a respected Hula-hula, while in another he acts as a hard-working Boru.
